newsitem.title: INDIA: Pipeline oil flow resumes to India refinery.
newsitem.headline: Pipeline oil flow resumes to India refinery.

text.p: The flow of crude oil to a refinery owned by Indian Oil Corp Ltd resumed on Friday after a pipeline damaged by suspected separatist militants was repaired, United News of India (UNI) said.

Suspected members of the United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) on Thursday damaged the main crude oil pipeline to the Barauni refinery in the eastern state of Bihar. Barauni has an annual processing capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.
State-run Oil India Ltd (OIL) had said the refinery kept operating and had enough oil for two to three days.
UNI said OIL resumed pumping oil to the refinery on Friday afternoon.
Crude oil from the eastern area of nearby Assam state is pumped to the Barauni refinery through a 1,157 km (718 mile) pipeline.
Last year ULFA guerrillas bombed three oil pipelines some 50 km (30 miles) west of the Assam state capital Guwahati, forcing Barauni and another refinery to shut down temporarily.
The leftist ULFA is fighting a decade-old campaign for an independent socialist state. ULFA's main targets are officials, security forces and tea planters.
